Fall Maple Leaf Garland with Pumpkins and Acorns 🍂🍁

A cozy fall garland with crochet maple leaves in orange, mustard, cream, and rust, plus little pumpkins and acorns — all strung on jute twine for warm October days.

I made this one on a golden October afternoon with warm sunlight coming through my window — I had real maple leaves on my table, just like in your photo with orange, yellow, cream, and rust leaves hanging on jute twine, and tiny pumpkins and acorns dangling between them. A friend who loves fall decor asked for a garland that wasn't store-bought — "Can you make one with leaves and little pumpkins?" So I sat at my wooden table with orange, mustard, cream, rust, brown yarn, jute twine, and my tea steaming beside me, and crocheted leaves while pampas grass swayed behind. By evening it was hanging on my white wall with fairy lights twinkling, and it made my whole room feel like fall.

Level Beginner — maple leaves + tiny pumpkins + acorns — weekend make
Yarn Worsted — orange 40g, mustard yellow 30g, cream 30g, rust/burnt orange 30g, brown 20g, orange-brown for pumpkins 20g — 4.0mm hook for leaves, 3.5mm for pumpkins/acorns — jute twine 6 feet
Size Garland about 5 feet long — maple leaves about 4" wide ×4.5" tall — pumpkins about 1.5" wide — acorns about 1.2" tall — 7 leaves + 4 pumpkins + 3 acorns

My yarn basket — orange, mustard, cream, rust, brown with jute twine

For this garland I used worsted weight yarn — pumpkin orange 40 grams, mustard yellow 30 grams, cream 30 grams, rust/burnt orange 30 grams for maple leaves, warm brown 20 grams and orange-brown 20 grams for little pumpkins and acorns. I use a 4.0mm hook for leaves so they are soft and drapey with textured stitches — and a 3.5mm hook for tiny pumpkins and acorns so they are neat — about 1.5" wide for pumpkins and 1.2" tall for acorns. I also had jute twine 6 feet long for stringing — natural twine — just like in your photo with jute twine holding orange, yellow, cream, rust leaves and little pumpkins and acorns.

My yarn basket — orange, mustard yellow, cream, rust, and brown yarn balls with wooden hook, jute twine, and autumn maple leaves on white wooden table — beginning of fall garland — real photo.

I use warm fall colors — orange, mustard, cream, rust — not bright neon — they look cozy with warm sunlight and pampas grass behind like in your photo.

How this garland is made — leaves + pumpkins + acorns on twine

This garland is simple — you crochet 7 maple leaves — about 4" wide ×4.5" tall each — in different fall colors — orange, mustard, cream, rust — 2 orange, 2 mustard, 1 cream, 2 rust — 7 leaves total — then 4 little pumpkins — about 1.5" wide each — 2 orange and 2 cream — and 3 acorns — about 1.2" tall each — brown — then you string them all on jute twine 6 feet long, alternating leaves and pumpkins/acorns — leaf, pumpkin, leaf, acorn, leaf — so the garland is about 5 feet long with items spaced about 6" apart.

Maple leaves — make 7 — 4" wide

MAPLE LEAVES — 4.0MM — 4 INCH WIDE — MAKE 7
Maple leaf — worsted, 4.0mm hook — one leaf about 4" wide ×4.5" tall:
Ch 2 — magic ring alternative — or ch 12 for center stem chain
Row 1: ch 12 — this is center stem and middle vein — 12 chains — about 3" long — stem at bottom
Row 2: sc in 2nd chain from hook, hdc, dc, dc, dc, hdc, hdc, sc, sc, sl st, sc in last chain for tip — 11 sts along one side of chain — working around chain
Row 3: working other side of same chain — sc, hdc, dc 3, hdc 2, sc 2, sl st, ch 4 for first side lobe — turn — side lobe — sc in 2nd chain, hdc, dc, dc — 4 sts — lobe about 1" tall
Row 4: sl st back to center chain, ch 5 for second side lobe — sc in 2nd chain, hdc, dc, dc, hdc — 5 sts — lobe about 1.2" tall
Row 5: sl st back to center, ch 4 for third lobe tip — repeat for total 5 lobes — 2 small bottom lobes 0.8", 2 middle lobes 1.2", 1 top lobe 1.5" tall — maple leaf shape — 5 points
Edge: sc around entire leaf — about 28 sc around edge — gives clean edge — adds texture — like real maple leaf in your photo with textured knit look
Stem: ch 4, sl st 3 — tiny stem 0.6" at bottom — leaf about 4" wide ×4.5" tall including stem
Make 7 leaves — 2 orange, 2 mustard yellow, 1 cream, 2 rust/burnt orange — each 4" wide ×4.5" tall — textured maple leaves like in your photo with 5 lobes and center vein

Each maple leaf is a center chain 12 long — about 3" — with side lobes crocheted off it — 5 lobes total — 2 small bottom 0.8" tall, 2 middle 1.2" tall, 1 top 1.5" tall — plus tiny stem ch4 sl st 3 — 0.6" at bottom — leaf about 4" wide ×4.5" tall including stem — with textured edge of 28 sc around — looks like real maple leaf with center vein — like in your photo where orange, yellow, cream, rust maple leaves have textured knit look and little stems. I make 7 leaves — 2 orange, 2 mustard, 1 cream, 2 rust.

Orange maple leaf in progress — orange yarn half maple leaf with wooden hook and orange yarn ball on wooden table with notebook that says "Maple leaf - row 8, inc in tips, 12 dc around" and scissors — real photo — leaf about 4" wide.

Little pumpkins — make 4 — 1.5" wide

PUMPKINS — ORANGE + CREAM — 3.5MM — 1.5 INCH WIDE — MAKE 4
Little pumpkins — orange and cream, 3.5mm hook — make 4:
R1: magic ring, 6 sc — 6
R2: inc 6 — 12
R3: [sc, inc]6 — 18
R4: [sc 2, inc]6 — 24 — widest about 1.5" wide — 24 sts
R5-7: sc 24 — 3 rounds straight — pumpkin body about 0.8" tall — 24 each round
R8: [sc 2, dec]6 — 18
R9: [sc, dec]6 — 12 — stuff lightly
R10: dec 6 — 6 — close with needle — leave long tail 18" — wrap tail around outside 5 times pulling gently for 5 ridges — like real pumpkin — tie — pumpkin 1.5" wide ×1" tall with 5 sections
Stem — brown, 3.5mm — ch 4, sc 3 — 0.6" stem — sew on top center
Make 4 pumpkins — 2 orange, 2 cream/beige — each 1.5" wide — 5 ridges — for garland

Pumpkins are tiny balls 6→24 — widest 1.5" wide — 3 rounds straight at 24 sts — body 0.8" tall — decrease 24→12→6 close — wrap 5 times for 5 ridges — 1.5" wide ×1" tall with brown stem 0.6" — make 4 — 2 orange and 2 cream/beige — like in your photo where orange and cream pumpkins hang between maple leaves — 1.5" wide each.

Little orange pumpkins and brown acorns — four tiny orange pumpkins with green stems and brown yarn ball and orange yarn ball on wooden table with real acorns scattered — fresh real photo — pumpkins 1.5" wide, acorns 1.2" tall.

Acorns — make 3 — 1.2" tall

ACORNS — BROWN — 3.5MM — 1.2 INCH TALL — MAKE 3
Acorns — brown, 3.5mm hook — make 3 — 1.2" tall:
Cap — light brown/beige, 3.5mm — textured — 6→12→18 — sc 18×2 rounds with bobble texture for acorn cap texture — cap about 0.6" tall, 1" wide
Body — dark brown, 3.5mm — 6→12→18 — sc 18×3 rounds — body about 0.8" tall — dec 18→12→6 close — cap overlaps body about 0.4" like real acorn, so total height is about 1.2" tall, 0.8" wide — sew cap to body
Stem — brown — ch 3, sl st 2 — 0.4" tiny stem on top of cap
Make 3 acorns — each 1.2" tall, 0.8" wide — brown caps with texture — like in your photo with little acorns hanging between leaves and pumpkins

Acorns are tiny — cap light brown/beige 6→18 — 2 rounds at 18 with bobble texture for acorn cap texture — cap 0.6" tall, 1" wide — body dark brown 6→18 — 3 rounds at 18 — body 0.8" tall — dec to close — total with overlap 1.2" tall, 0.8" wide — cap overlaps body 0.4" like real acorn — tiny stem ch3 sl st 2 — 0.4" — make 3 brown acorns — like in your photo with little acorns hanging on jute twine between maple leaves.

Assembly — stringing garland on jute twine

ASSEMBLY — 6 FEET JUTE TWINE — 5 FEET LONG GARLAND
Assembly — string garland on jute twine 6 feet:
1. Cut jute twine 6 feet long — 72" — leaves 6" extra on each end for hanging loops — garland will be about 5 feet long — 60" — with items spaced about 6" apart
2. Maple leaves — 7 leaves — 4" wide ×4.5" tall — 2 orange, 2 mustard, 1 cream, 2 rust — spaced about 6" apart along twine
3. Pumpkins — 4 pumpkins — 1.5" wide — 2 orange, 2 cream — between leaves
4. Acorns — 3 acorns — 1.2" tall — brown — between leaves and pumpkins
5. Pattern along twine: start with maple leaf orange, pumpkin orange, maple leaf mustard, acorn brown, maple leaf cream, pumpkin cream, maple leaf rust, acorn, maple leaf orange, pumpkin orange, maple leaf mustard, pumpkin cream, maple leaf rust, acorn — alternating leaves and pumpkins/acorns — 7 leaves + 4 pumpkins + 3 acorns =14 items — 6 feet jute twine gives 72" total, minus 6" each end for hanging loops =60" usable — 13 gaps between 14 items — 60" ÷13 ≈4.6" apart — spaced about 4.5-5" apart — 5 feet long garland
6. Attach each item to twine — use long tail — tie around twine with 2 knots — or ch6 loop at top of leaf and thread twine through loop — secure — leaves hang with stem down — pumpkins and acorns hang with stem up
7. Make hanging loops at ends — tie loop 2" diameter at each end of twine — for hanging on wall or mantel

I string the garland on jute twine 6 feet long — 72" total — with 6" extra on each end for hanging loops, leaving 60" usable for items — so finished garland is about 5 feet long — 60" — with 14 items — 7 maple leaves 4" wide, 4 pumpkins 1.5" wide, 3 acorns 1.2" tall — 13 gaps between 14 items — 60" ÷13 ≈4.6" — spaced about 4.5-5" apart along twine — pattern alternating leaves and pumpkins/acorns — starting with orange maple leaf, then orange pumpkin, mustard leaf, acorn, cream leaf, cream pumpkin, rust leaf, acorn, orange leaf, orange pumpkin, mustard leaf, cream pumpkin, rust leaf, acorn — so colors alternate orange, mustard, cream, rust — like in your photo where orange, yellow, cream, rust maple leaves and orange and cream pumpkins and brown acorns hang on jute twine on white wall with warm sunlight and pampas grass behind.

Assembly — fall garland with orange and yellow maple leaves and orange pumpkins being strung on jute twine on white wall with warm sunlight — hands tying twine — real photo — garland about 5 feet long in progress.

Finished — fall maple leaf garland with pumpkins and acorns

And here it is — my cozy fall garland — about 5 feet long — 6 feet jute twine with 6" hanging loops on ends — with 7 maple leaves — each about 4" wide ×4.5" tall — 2 orange, 2 mustard yellow, 1 cream, 2 rust/burnt orange — textured with center vein and 5 lobes and tiny stems — plus 4 little pumpkins — 1.5" wide each — 2 orange and 2 cream with brown stems — and 3 little acorns — 1.2" tall each — brown with textured caps — all strung on jute twine with items spaced about 5-6" apart — like in your photo with orange, yellow, cream, rust maple leaves and orange and cream pumpkins and brown acorns hanging on jute twine on white wall with warm sunlight, pampas grass, and blurred cozy room behind.

Finished — fall maple leaf garland with crochet maple leaves in orange, mustard yellow, cream, rust/burnt orange — 4" wide each — plus little orange and cream pumpkins 1.5" wide and brown acorns 1.2" tall — all strung on jute twine about 5 feet long — hanging on white wall with warm sunlight, pampas grass, and cozy blurred room — cozy fall decor. 🍂🍁

When I hung it on my white wall next morning with warm sunlight coming in and pampas grass behind, my friend said, "Did you make that garland? The little pumpkins and acorns between the leaves are so cute!" I laughed and said, "I made it yesterday with tea and maple leaves on my table." I hope you make yours on a cozy fall afternoon too — maybe with maple leaves and pumpkins nearby — and hang it on your wall, mantel, or window for warm October days.

— Sara
